Unilateral bow-leg c̅ a history of prior injury to that limb → malunion of an old fracture.
Achilles tendon rupture → positive Thompson (Simmonds) test (no plantarflexion on calf squeeze).
Compartment syndrome → emergency fasciotomy; absent pulse is a late sign.
Supracondylar fracture → anterior interosseous nerve (median branch) injury → can't make 'OK' sign.
Hypercalcemia c̅ diffuse bone loss → primary hyperparathyroidism; sestamibi scan localises the adenoma.
Periosteal reaction c̅ medullary involvement: MRI defines extent before biopsy.

Anterior shoulder dislocation: arm abducted & externally rotated.
Posterior: adducted & internally rotated.

Equinus – plantar flexion; planus – flat arch
Cavus – high arch (extended dorsally); calcaneus – dorsiflexion
